rationale: This WorkUnit has no physical boundary events. No synthetic occurrence is introduced merely to represent the found output; io.found and io.found_idx are registered selector-result signals rather than protocol milestones.
A1 exactly captures the function implemented by ForwardingAgeLogic. The candidate set is the eight bits of io.matches and the pivot is io.youngest.

The RTL constructs age_mask[i] as true exactly when i < io.youngest, then constructs a 16-bit vector Cat(io.matches & age_mask, io.matches). Because the subsequent assignments inspect bits 0 through 15 in increasing order and later assignments override earlier assignments, the highest set bit in this expanded vector determines found_idx.

That implementation is equivalent to strict cyclic_predecessor selection around io.youngest: it first prefers io.youngest-1 and proceeds downward toward zero, then wraps to entry 7 and continues downward, with io.youngest itself last.

If at least one candidate exists below the pivot, the greatest matching index below io.youngest wins. Otherwise the greatest matching index in the wrapped portion wins. This is precisely the cyclic predecessor semantics rather than ordinary linear_max.
found_match and found_idx are concrete registers, while io.found and io.found_idx are direct outputs of those registers. Therefore latency_cycles is exactly one.

Neither found_match nor found_idx has a grounded reset value in the supplied ledger. initialization.kind is therefore implicit_unconstrained; imposing found=false or found_idx=0 initially would add an unsupported RTL guarantee.

The zero assignments to found_match and found_idx are next-state defaults for each selector evaluation, not reset initialization. They ensure that an empty sampled candidate set yields found=false after the one-cycle delay.

No identity key is required. The selected finite index itself is the result of the priority operation, and the indexed_priority_select axiom directly relates that result to the sampled candidate vector.
No fairness or liveness property is involved.
